assessment.weighting: Spring 1 units (equations, rearranging, coordinates and straight line graphs, inequalities, shape properties and angles in polygons) and Spring 2 units (proportion and real life graphs). A Spring 1 test covers only the Spring 1 units: untick Spring 2 in Progress until they are taught. Sparx codes on each card lead to the videos.

mock.note: 25 questions over the units you have studied. Work on paper.

units.name: Shape properties and angles in polygons

cards.title: Solving one and two step equations
cards.question: How do you solve linear equations? (Sparx videos: M707, M509)
points: Do the same to both sides to keep the equation balanced.
Undo in reverse order: 3x + 5 = 20 → 3x = 15 → x = 5.
Check by substituting your answer back in.
cards.watch_out: Write each step under the last one, with the equals signs lined up.
cards.hook: Balance: what you do to one side, do to the other.
cards.grade9: Leave answers as fractions if they are not whole, such as x = 7/3.

cards.title: Brackets and unknowns on both sides
cards.question: How do you solve equations with brackets or with x on both sides? (Sparx videos: M509)
points: Brackets: expand first. 2(x + 3) = 14 → 2x + 6 = 14 → x = 4.
Both sides: move the smaller x term. 5x − 3 = 2x + 9 → 3x − 3 = 9 → 3x = 12 → x = 4.
Collect x terms on one side and numbers on the other.
cards.grade9: Move the smaller x term to avoid negative x terms.

cards.title: Forming equations
cards.question: How do you write and solve an equation from a worded problem or shape? (Sparx videos: M957)
points: Let x be the unknown, write an expression for each part, then set up an equation.
Angles in a triangle add to 180°: x + 2x + 30 = 180 → 3x = 150 → x = 50.
Perimeter: add all the sides and set equal to the total.

example.heading: Worked example
lines: I think of a number, double it and add 7. The answer is 31.

cards.watch_out: Answer the question asked, which may be an angle, not x.
cards.grade9: State what x represents at the start.

cards.title: Rearranging formulae
cards.question: How do you change the subject of a formula? (Sparx video: M242)
points: The subject is the letter on its own, such as v in v = u + at.
Undo operations in reverse order, doing the same to both sides, just like solving an equation.
Make a the subject of v = u + at: v − u = at, so a = (v − u) ÷ t.
Make r the subject of C = 2πr: r = C ÷ 2π.
cards.watch_out: Undo the operation done last first. In P = 2l + 2w, subtract 2w before dividing by 2.
cards.grade9: Check by putting numbers in: if v = 10, u = 4 and t = 2, then a = 3, and 4 + 3 × 2 = 10.

cards.title: Coordinates and straight lines
cards.question: What do the lines x = a, y = b and y = x look like? (Sparx videos: M618, M797)
points: Coordinates are written (x, y): along the corridor, then up the stairs.
x = 3 is a vertical line through 3 on the x-axis. y = 2 is a horizontal line.
y = x goes diagonally through the origin. y = −x goes the other way.
cards.watch_out: x = a is vertical, which feels backwards. Every point on it has x = a.
cards.hook: Along the corridor and up the stairs.
cards.grade9: Find where two lines cross by reading or by solving.

cards.title: Plotting linear graphs
cards.question: How do you plot a straight-line graph from an equation? (Sparx videos: M932)
points: Make a table of values, for example x = −2 to 3.
Substitute each x into the equation. y = 2x + 1: x = 0 → 1; x = 2 → 5.
Plot the points and join them with a ruler, extending across the grid.
cards.watch_out: If one point is not in line, recheck that calculation.
cards.grade9: Use three or more points so you can spot errors.

cards.title: Gradient and y-intercept, y = mx + c
cards.question: What do m and c tell you in y = mx + c, and how do you find the gradient? (Sparx videos: M544, M888)
points: m is the gradient (steepness): change in y ÷ change in x.
c is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis.
y = 3x − 2: gradient 3, crosses at (0, −2).
Parallel lines have the same gradient. A negative gradient slopes downwards.

example.heading: Gradient between (1, 4) and (3, 10)
lines: change in y = 6, change in x = 2

cards.watch_out: Rearrange into y = ... first. 2y = 4x + 6 becomes y = 2x + 3.
cards.hook: m for move (steepness), c for crosses (the y-axis).
cards.grade9: Find the equation of a line from two points, gradient first, then substitute to find c.

cards.title: Inequalities on number lines
cards.question: How do you show and solve inequalities on a number line? (Sparx video: M384)
points: Symbols: < less than, > greater than, ≤ less than or equal to, ≥ greater than or equal to.
Open circle for < and > (the number is not included). Filled circle for ≤ and ≥ (it is included).
−2 < x ≤ 3: open circle at −2, filled circle at 3, line between them. Integers: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3.
Solve like an equation: 2x + 1 > 7 gives 2x > 6, so x > 3.
cards.watch_out: x > 3 does not include 3. The smallest whole number it allows is 4.
cards.hook: The crocodile mouth eats the bigger number.
cards.grade9: List the integers that satisfy two inequalities at once by drawing both on one number line.

cards.title: Properties of 2D shapes
cards.question: What are the properties of the special triangles and quadrilaterals? (Sparx video: M276)
points: Triangles: equilateral (3 equal sides, 3 angles of 60°), isosceles (2 equal sides and 2 equal angles), scalene (no equal sides), right angled.
Square: 4 equal sides, 4 right angles. Rectangle: opposite sides equal, 4 right angles.
Parallelogram: opposite sides equal and parallel, opposite angles equal. Rhombus: a parallelogram with 4 equal sides.
Trapezium: one pair of parallel sides. Kite: two pairs of equal adjacent sides, one pair of equal angles.
cards.watch_out: A square is also a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram, because it has all their properties.
cards.grade9: Use properties as reasons in angle questions, such as base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

cards.title: Angles in polygons
cards.question: How do you find interior and exterior angles of polygons? (Sparx video: M653)
points: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides. A hexagon: 4 × 180 = 720°.
Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°.
Regular polygon: each exterior angle = 360 ÷ n; interior angle = 180 − exterior angle.
Regular pentagon: exterior 360 ÷ 5 = 72°, interior 180 − 72 = 108°.
cards.watch_out: The (n − 2) × 180 formula gives the total of all interior angles, not one angle.
cards.hook: Split into triangles: a polygon with n sides makes n − 2 triangles.
cards.grade9: Work backwards: if each exterior angle is 30°, the polygon has 360 ÷ 30 = 12 sides.

cards.title: Direct proportion and the unitary method
cards.question: How do you solve direct proportion problems? (Sparx video: M681)
points: Direct proportion: when one amount doubles, the other doubles too.
Unitary method: find the value of one, then multiply. 5 pens cost £3.50, so 1 pen costs 70p and 8 pens cost £5.60.
Recipes: a recipe for 4 uses 300 g of flour, so for 6 use 300 ÷ 4 × 6 = 450 g.
Best buy: compare the price of one unit, such as price per 100 g.
cards.watch_out: Check the answer is sensible: more items should cost more in direct proportion.
cards.grade9: Write a full comparison sentence in best buy questions, such as the 500 g bag is cheaper per 100 g.

cards.title: Inverse proportion and proportion graphs
cards.question: What is inverse proportion, and what do proportion graphs look like? (Sparx videos: M478, M448)
points: Inverse proportion: when one amount doubles, the other halves. More workers means less time.
3 painters take 8 hours, so the job is 24 painter hours. 4 painters take 24 ÷ 4 = 6 hours.
A direct proportion graph is a straight line through the origin (0, 0).
An inverse proportion graph is a curve that gets closer to both axes but never touches them.
cards.watch_out: A straight line that does not start at (0, 0) is not direct proportion.
cards.grade9: Decide first whether the amounts go up together or one goes up as the other goes down.

cards.title: Real life graphs
cards.question: How do you read and interpret real life graphs? (Sparx videos: M843, M771, M205)
points: Read the axes and units first, then read values across and down with a ruler.
Conversion graphs change one unit to another, such as pounds to euros or miles to km.
Distance time graphs: a flat line means stopped; a steeper line means faster. Gradient = speed.
Filling containers: a narrow part fills quickly (steep line); a wide part fills slowly (shallow line).
cards.watch_out: On a distance time graph, a line going back down means returning towards the start, not slowing.
cards.grade9: Use the gradient with units: 30 km in 0.5 hours is a speed of 60 km/h.

cards.title: Spring methods to remember
cards.question: Can you recall each key Spring method quickly?
points: Equations and rearranging: undo in reverse order, same on both sides.
y = mx + c: m is the gradient, c is the y-intercept.
Inequalities: open circle for < and >, filled for ≤ and ≥.
Polygons: interior sum (n − 2) × 180°; exterior angles add to 360°.
Proportion: direct, find one then multiply; inverse, multiply to find the total then divide.
cards.watch_out: Show working every time; method marks are given even if the final answer is wrong.
cards.grade9: Check each answer by substituting it back or estimating.

written.q: A rectangle has length 2x + 3 and width x. Its perimeter is 36 cm. Find x and the length.
Find the equation of the straight line through (1, 5) and (3, 11).
Work out the size of each interior angle of a regular octagon.
A 400 g jar of jam costs £1.60 and a 650 g jar costs £2.47. Which is the better value? Show your working.
model: The 650 g jar is better value (1)

exam_tips.timing: Spend about 1 minute per mark. Show working on paper even in an online test.
section_a: Write the equation or formula before you put numbers in.
Read the axes and units before you read a graph.
Use a ruler for every line on a graph.
section_b: Show every step; most marks are for method.
Give reasons for angle answers, such as exterior angles add to 360°.
Check by substituting answers back in.
grade9: Decide first whether amounts are in direct or inverse proportion, then choose the method.
Say what a gradient means in the real situation: 60 km/h, not just 60.
Check each angle answer is sensible: an interior angle of a regular polygon is always less than 180°.
week: Most days, 10 to 15 minutes: press Start today (due cards, the new batch, then a short quiz).
Once a week, 10 minutes: take one real price change (a sale or a bigger pack) and work out the better buy with proportion, saying why. Then one Written practice question with every step shown.
Once a week: a quiz on the Quiz tab that mixes older units with this week's, so earlier topics stay in.
Fix one mistake: rewrite one wrong answer or one watch out from memory, then check it against the card.

vocab.meaning: A statement that two things are equal, with an unknown to find
The letter on its own on one side of a formula
vocab.example: In v = u + at, v is the subject.

vocab.meaning: How steep a line is: change in y ÷ change in x
vocab.example: A steeper line has a bigger gradient.

vocab.meaning: Where a line crosses an axis
A statement that one amount is bigger or smaller than another
A closed 2D shape with straight sides
vocab.example: A hexagon is a polygon with six sides.
Each interior angle of a square is 90°.

vocab.meaning: When two amounts change at the same rate
